subject: Clarify staged notification commitments / data custody handoff for suspected exfiltration
messages:
From: security@lnksys.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@lnksys.com
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Potential data exposure — request for DPA notification timing and evidence custody

Hi Jonas,

We’ve detected suspicious activity in our environment that may have touched inference logs routed to Redwood’s hosted endpoint. At this stage we are treating it as a potential data exposure. Our security team needs to understand: under the current DPA, what are Redwood’s notification timelines (internal triage vs. customer notice), what evidence retention windows do you commit to for forensic snapshots, and how will you coordinate with our forensics team for cross-border exports?

Please treat this as urgent. We’d like a proposed staged response and any immediate asks from our side. I’ve CC’d procurement because we may need to sign a short amendment for expanded evidence transfer.

Attachments: none (initial alert).

— Alex Rivera
Head of Security Operations, LNK Systems
security@lnksys.com
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: security@lnksys.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for DPA notification timing and evidence custody

Alex — thanks for flagging and sorry to hear this. High level proposal from Redwood:

1) Immediate: we’ll open an internal incident (INF-7892) and begin triage now. We will preserve server and KV cache snapshots related to the LNK tenant immediately and place a 30-day hold (extendable) on any logs/metadata streams.

2) 48-hour assessment window: we commit to a preliminary impact assessment within 48 hours (scope, affected object ids, cursory TLP=AMBER summary). This is to avoid premature customer notices for false positives.

3) 72-hour external notice target: if assessment confirms customer-impacting exposure, Redwood will notify affected customers within 72 hours (subject to law enforcement requests and cross-border restrictions).

4) Forensics export: we can provide exported forensic snapshots under an encrypted transfer (customer KMS or Redwoods’ OF-escrow flow). Cross-border transfers will be coordinated per DPA Section 6, with a formal chain-of-custody manifest and a one-week evidence retention guarantee once exported.

Immediate asks from LNK:
- Point of contact for your forensics (name, PGP key or SFTP key).
- Any legal hold instructions or external counsel contact.

I’m looping Kimberly (legal) for DPA amendments and Ben (security) for export/forensic specifics. We’ll follow up with a proposed amendment and a matrix of evidence we can export.

— Jonas
Director, Incident Response — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, security@lnksys.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for DPA notification timing and evidence custody

Alex / team — quick legal note on DPA commitments and a proposed short-form amendment:

- Current DPA: section 4.2 (Incident Notification) requires "without undue delay" and cooperation for evidence transfer. That language is intentionally flexible; for operational clarity we propose adding a short appendix that defines:
  * "Preliminary assessment" = delivery of a scope summary within 48 hours,
  * "Customer notice" = notification within 72 hours of confirmation of personal data exposure,
  * "Forensic export" = Redwood will retain a copy for 7 days after transfer and may extend upon written request.

- Subprocessor angle: we can confirm the active subprocessor list within 24 hours and include a commitment that Redwood will require downstream subprocessors to maintain the same 7-day hold and export cooperation as Redwood. We cannot assume liability for subprocessors’ independent breaches but will enforce contractual cooperation clauses and expedite audits.

I’ve drafted an amendment (attached) that courts these points and preserves Redwood’s ability to pause notices pending law enforcement. If LNK is comfortable, sign and we can turn on the export workflow.

Attachment: DPA_amendment_PROPOSED_v1.pdf

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: security@lnksys.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for DPA notification timing and evidence custody

Alex — technical follow-up on the export and custody plan:

- Evidence we can stage immediately: per-tenant inference logs (rotating), model input/output digests, KV-cache snapshots (timebound), and orchestration traces.
- Export mechanism options:
  1) Encrypted SFTP to LNK’s supplied host/key (preferred for immediate access),
  2) Customer-managed KMS-encrypted S3 share (requires cross-account role; longer to provision),
  3) Escrow snapshot via third-party forensic escrow (we have partners; requires signed amendment).

- Retention: we will hold an internal copy for 30 days by default. For exported evidence we commit to a 7-day post-transfer retention for handoff verification unless LNK requests extended custody with a specific retention window.

- Small operational ask: before any export we need written authorization from LNK’s security POC and confirmation of export destination details. Also requesting a contact for any cross-border export approvals if exports will leave the EU.

I’ve attached a matrix of the fields we can export and approximate sizes.

Attachment: forensic_evidence_matrix.xlsx

— Ben Carter
Head of Security Operations — Redwood Inference
From: security@lnksys.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-06T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for DPA notification timing and evidence custody

Thanks Jonas / Kimberly / Ben — appreciate the quick answers. LNK can:

- Provide a named forensics lead (Maya Chen) with an SFTP public key within 2 hours.
- Accept an initial 7-day hold on exported evidence; procurement will review a 30-day extension if needed.
- Sign a focused DPA appendix agreeing the 48h/72h/7-day definitions — procurement will need a DocuSign link.

We do have one substantive question on subprocessors: if Redwood’s downstream TPU vendor (VendorX) is involved in log retention, will Redwood be the party to request the evidence snapshot from VendorX or will LNK need to serve VendorX directly? We prefer Redwood to act as the liaison so we don’t have to disclose our legal processes to multiple vendors.

Attachment: none.

— Alex Rivera
Head of Security Operations, LNK Systems
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: security@lnksys.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-07T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — request for DPA notification timing and evidence custody

Alex / team — quick confirmation and action items:

1) Redwood will act as primary liaison to subprocessors. We will issue internal subpoenas/requests to VendorX and any other downstream processors to collect the required snapshots and then provide a consolidated export to LNK. We will include chain-of-custody manifests for each subprocessor response.

2) DocuSign: Kimberly’s amendment attached as a short-form appendix will go to Alex/procurement. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/lnk/XYZ123-AMEND (attached).

3) Export plan: Ben will initiate SFTP transfer upon receipt of Maya Chen’s key and written export authorization. Ben: please open an internal runbook ticket INF-7892-EXPORT and log cross-border approvals if the export requires EU clearance.

4) Notification cadence: Redwood will produce a preliminary scope report by 2026-08-07T18:00:00-07:00 and, if confirmed, an external customer notice target of 2026-08-08T14:00:00-07:00 (we will be careful to align with law enforcement delays).

I’ve attached the DocuSign stub and will send the amendment to procurement now. Please reply if any changes.

Attachments: docsign-lnksys-amendment.link.txt

— Jonas Weber
Director, Incident Response — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
